body.target_estimand: \(\bigl(\mathbf 1\{X=a_X\text{ is a Beckers cause of }Y=a_Y\},C^\star(I)\bigr)\), where \(C^\star(I)=\min\bigl(\{\sum_{e\in E(G)\setminus E(H)}c(e):(H,w)\text{ is a canonical Beckers witness}\}\cup\{+\infty\}\bigr)\).
body.estimand_functional: On instances covered by \(\texttt{thm:relevant-component-polynomial-frontier}\), let \(C_X,C_Y\) be the weak components of \(X,Y\), and for their common component put \(r(C)=|E(G[C])|-|C|+1\). Then \(C^\star(I)=+\infty\) if \(C_X\ne C_Y\); if \(r(C)=0\), \(C^\star(I)=\min_{s_i\in R(P_i)\setminus\{a_{P_i}\}}\sum_{i=1}^{m}C_i(s_{i-1},s_i)\); and if \(r(C)=1\), \(C^\star(I)=\min_b\min_{w\in R(C)}\{\sum_{Z\in V\cap C}\Phi_Z^b(w_Z,w_{\operatorname{Pa}_{G[C]}(Z)})+\sum_{q\in C}\psi_q(w_q)\}\), with \(b,\Phi^b,\psi\) the explicit exceptional-edge modes and local potentials in \(\texttt{lem:connected-unicycle-min-sum}\). In all cases the causal indicator equals \(\mathbf 1\{C^\star(I)<+\infty\}\).

sampling_model.design: No statistical sampling; the input is one explicitly encoded finite acyclic NSCM and one designated actual solution.
sampling_model.units: Vertices, domain values, local-table rows, output incidences, graph edges, and rational cost records counted by \(L\).
sampling_model.treatment: The singleton counterfactual intervention changes \(X=a_X\) to some \(X=x'\ne a_X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; local tables are total and all finite domains are explicitly enumerated.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the local relations are supplied exactly rather than estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, proved on page 532, gives a same-signature representative that is both a structural simplification of the original model and a witness to the actual-cause counterfactual dependence.
Acyclic nondeterministic SCMs use set-valued mechanisms and preserve the designated actual solution under counterfactual evaluation.
Bounded-domain, bounded-width causal trees and layered graphs permit polynomial Halpern--Pearl cause decisions.
Halpern--Pearl weak and actual cause problems have definition-dependent hardness classifications.
The updated Halpern--Pearl definition changes the exact complexity of computing actual causes.
Binary acyclic Halpern--Pearl actual-cause checking can be encoded as satisfiability.
Binary Halpern--Pearl checking and inference can be formulated as ILP and MaxSAT optimization.
Adjustable beam search approximately identifies Halpern--Pearl-style causes in non-Boolean and stochastic systems.

body.tldr: Beckers defines actual causation by counterfactual dependence in an actualized structural simplification, but does not provide an exact algorithmic frontier. For finite explicit local tables, tractability localizes to the weak component of the full graph on \(U\cup V\) containing the query: different components give an immediate negative cut; cycle rank zero gives the exact linear-arithmetic value-path compiler; and cycle rank one gives an exact exceptional-edge min-sum algorithm with positive, optimum, and separating certificates, while all other components may be arbitrary. A shared-selector reduction proves NP-completeness even for deterministic binary models whose endogenous graph is one directed chain, so hardness transfers to the broader Beckers class having the published endogenous causal-tree graph shape. This transfers only graph shape and does not conflate Beckers with Halpern--Pearl semantics.

project_justification.gap: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, with proof on page 532, of Beckers2025Actual supplies a same-signature structural-simplification representative but no compiler, certificate system, minimum-cost result, or complexity classification. Existing causal-tree algorithms and SAT encodings concern Halpern--Pearl causation and do not enforce Beckers's full-graph reachability legality or actual-row freezing.
project_justification.niche: The novel computational scope uses finite explicitly encoded tables and restricts only the weak full-graph component shared by \(X\) and \(Y\) to cycle rank at most one. Component separation leaves every other weak component unrestricted. The condition is on the full graph over \(U\cup V\), not on the endogenous graph \(G[V]\) used by the published Halpern--Pearl causal-tree result.
project_justification.fill: The project proves an extensional forest compiler, an exact relevant-component frontier through cycle rank one, explicit additive min-sum functionals, and independently checkable positive, optimality, and negative certificates. The selector-and-clause reduction proves Beckers NP-completeness on a deterministic binary endogenous chain and therefore on the broader endogenous-tree graph-shape class, while the shared-selector obstruction explains why endogenous-only propagation cannot audit full-graph deletion legality.

body.related_work: Beckers2025Actual, Section 5.1, Definitions 13, 15, and 16 on pages 523--524 and Section 6, Definitions 18 and 19 and Proposition 20 on page 525, supplies the structural-simplification and actual-causation semantics; the proof of Proposition 20 appears on page 532. It is semantic prior art and contains no compiler, exact cost functional, or tractability frontier. Beckers2025NCM supplies set-valued equations and topological counterfactual semantics, while finite explicit encoding is a new computational-scope restriction here. The earlier UAI version of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3, propagates families of endogenous path-value sets for Halpern--Pearl causes on causal trees. The positive result here instead restricts the query-relevant weak component of the full graph on \(U\cup V\) to cycle rank at most one and explicitly audits actualized projection and deleted-edge reachability. The hardness reduction has a directed-chain endogenous graph, so its graph shape lies inside the published endogenous causal-tree shape and transfers NP-hardness upward for Beckers semantics; it does not transfer or alter the Halpern--Pearl theorem. EiterLukasiewicz2002Complexity and AleksandrowiczEtAl2014 show that complexity is definition-sensitive, but neither treats Beckers deletion. IbrahimRehwaldPretschner2019SAT and IbrahimPretschner2020Optimization concern Boolean Halpern--Pearl encodings, and ReydDiaconescuDessalles2025Search gives approximate Halpern--Pearl-style search rather than exact Beckers certificates. No semantic equivalence between these causal definitions is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact positive frontier proved here stops when the weak full-graph component containing \(X\) and \(Y\) has cycle rank at least two. No claim is made for general full-graph treewidth FPT, succinct mechanisms, continuous domains, negative deletion costs, unrestricted polynomial negative certificates, or unrestricted parsimonious certificate counting. The selector reduction gives a bijection only for normalized certificates; unrestricted successful retained graphs may encode one satisfying assignment in several ways and normalization need not preserve a counting interpretation.
body.honest_scope: The proved result assumes finite nonempty domains, total explicitly listed set-valued tables, an acyclic full graph, a supplied actual solution, and nonnegative rational deletion costs. It localizes the full-graph restriction: only the weak component containing both query variables must have cycle rank at most one, and distinct query components are certified negative; other components may be arbitrary. This is not the published Eiter--Lukasiewicz endogenous causal-tree class, because shared exogenous roots participate in Beckers reachability legality. The deterministic binary endogenous-chain reduction nevertheless lies inside that published graph shape, so NP-hardness transfers upward only as a Beckers graph-class statement. Cycle rank at least two in the relevant full component, general treewidth parameterization, and unrestricted certificate counting remain outside the claims.
